svg.title: Clearway: what happens when the operator confirms or rejects an incident
svg.text: Both teach the incident memory. Confirm keeps the incident alive; Reject closes it and marks its look, at that spot, as harmless.
the service takes in new verdicts every 1 s
• no category yet (pending), or merged away
• Confirm after Reject (Reject after Confirm is allowed)
acknowledging or closing the alarm there
is not read back by Clearway:
only the board and the phone teach the memory
stays open and recurs as before;
a later Reject is still allowed
Hafnia's NONE looks at this spot
LATER: A CHANGE AT THE SAME SPOT
no request; a cleared alarm reopens as New
What the Confirm changes, and what it does not
• Before it, a change here that looked more like something Hafnia had rejected than like the card
was skipped. Now it joins the incident.
• The alarm still closes by itself 60 s after the spot clears, and reopens on a recurrence.
• Nothing is released: the change detector keeps watching the spot.
LATER: A CHANGE AT THE SAME SPOT
one request, linked to the card
same category → joins the rejected card
rejected by Hafnia; the spot is released
a different problem still gets through
